sentences.text: 1. CAN 1 of 2024 and CAN 2 of 2024 are treated to be  on the day's list.

2. CAN 1 of 2024 is an application for condonation of  delay in preferring the present appeal under Section 71(6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act,
 2006 (for short 'the 2006 Act').
 3.

Learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant,
 by placing reliance on the averments made in the  condonation application, submits that the delay  was occasioned for reasons beyond the control of  the appellant.

4. First, the authorized signatory of the appellant, who  was well-acquainted with the facts of the case and  was in charge of drafting the appeal, was not Adani Wilmar Limited vs Central Food Safety Officer on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174296996/
1  available at the relevant juncture due to some  personal difficulty.

sentences.text:
2 5. Subsequently, difficulties cropped up since the  Filing Department of this court was itself in some  doubt as to what heading the appeal would be  classified under.
6.

We find substance in the said contention, since the  matter initially came up before this Bench with a  report of the Stamp Reporter with regard to the  correct classification and this court had to  ascertain as to what would be the correct category,
 since no specific classification is allocated for  appeals under the 2006 Act.
7. Hence, we find sufficient cause for the delay in  preferring the appeal.
8. Accordingly, CAN 1 of 2024 is allowed, thereby  condoning the delay in preferring CRA (DB) 268 of  2025.
9. The appeal, being both on facts and law, is required  to be heard on merits on the grounds taken in the  Memorandum of Appeal and accordingly is  admitted and shall be heard on such grounds.

10. We also find that the other defects pointed out by  the Stamp Reporter have, in the meantime, been  cured by the appellant.

sentences.text: 11. Heard learned senior counsel appearing for the  appellant on CAN 2 of 2024.
12. For the present, learned senior counsel confines his  arguments to the aspect of the allegation of  "misbranding".
3 13. The short backdrop of the case is that there was an  inspection of certain samples of the product 'Rice  Bran Oil' sold by the appellant-Company by the  Food Analyst under the 2006 Act.

14. The report of the said analyst indicated that the  sample tested as 'sub-standard' and 'misbranded'.
15.

The said report came up before the Adjudicating  Officer who held that the sample suffered from  being sub-standard, although the Food Analyst's  finding, marking the sample as misbranded, was  set aside.

16. However, the Appellate Authority, in an appeal  preferred by the present appellant against the  portion of the Adjudicating Officers' order whereby  the sample of the appellant was termed to be sub-  standard, traversed beyond its jurisdiction and,
 apart from affirming the portion of the Adjudicating  Officer's order whereby the sample was held to be  sub-standard, also entered into the question as to Adani Wilmar Limited vs Central Food Safety Officer on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174296996/
3  whether there was misbranding and upset the  finding of the Adjudication Officer by reversing the  same and holding that the sample was  'misbranded' as well.
17.

sentences.text:
The first ground on which the Appellate Authority's  order is challenged is that the Appellate Authority  acted beyond its jurisdiction in taking up the issue  of misbranding afresh, in the absence of any  challenge to the said portion of the Adjudicating  4  Officer's order being thrown by the respondent- authority.
18.

The appellant's appeal was confined only to the sub-standard labelling of the sample and not on the misbranding aspect of it, since the latter issue had been decided in favour of the appellant by the Adjudicating Officer.

19. Learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant also points out from the recording in the impugned judgment itself that the respondent-authority appeared and submitted that it relied on the order of the learned Adjudicating Officer and according to the respondent-authority, the said order was legal and valid.

20. Thus, it is argued, the legality and validity of the Adjudicating Officer's order, to the extent that the allegation of 'misbranding' of the appellant's product was turned down, was also accepted by the respondent itself.
21. Upon hearing learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, we find that there is substance in such contentions of the appellant.

22. First, no appeal was preferred by the respondent- authority against the finding of the Adjudicating Officer turning down the allegation of misbranding of the appellant's product sample and the appellate authority acted prima facie beyond its jurisdiction in suo motu taking up the said aspect and reversing the finding of the Adjudicating Officer.

Unlike a regular appeal in a civil court, nothing akin to Order XLI Rule 22 or Rule 33 of the Adani Wilmar Limited vs Central Food Safety Officer on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174296996/
4 Code of Civil Procedure is available to an Appellate Authority under the 2006 Act.

entities.text: Adani Wilmar Limited vs Central Food Safety Officer on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 23. Secondly, the respondent-authority itself had supported the order of the Adjudicating Officer in an unqualified manner, thereby making it clear that they did not assail the misbranding aspect of the matter, which is evident from the recording of such submission in the Appellate Authority's order itself.

24. Thirdly, we find from the order of the Appellate Authority that prior to reversing the Adjudicating Officer's order on its finding on the aspect of misbranding, the reasons therefor ascribed by the Adjudicating Officer were not even adverted to by the Appellate Authority.
25.

The Appellate Authority, surprisingly, went directly to the report of the Food Analyst and,
without any independent assessment of the same, reversed the finding of the Adjudicating Authority on the count of misbranding.

26. Accordingly, there shall be a stay of operation of the impugned judgment dated April 5, 2024 passed by the Presiding Officer, West Bengal Food Safety Appellate Tribunal insofar as the Appellate Authority held that the appellant is guilty of misbranding its product within the contemplation of Section 52 of the 2006 Act, till disposal of the application.

entities.text: West Bengal Food Safety Appellate Tribunal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 27. It is made clear that the other aspect of the matter, regarding the allegation of the appellant's product being sub-standard, is left open for being finally decided at the hearing of the appeal.
28. We fix the appeal itself for hearing along with the application on the next date, that is, on August 12, 2025.
29. In view of all the relevant papers being substantially annexed to the connected application as well as the Memorandum of Appeal, the requirement of preparation of paper books is dispensed with.
30. Since the respondent has already entered appearance in the appeal, formal notice of appeal on the respondent is also dispensed with.
31. The appeal is treated to be ready for hearing and shall be heard on the papers already on record.

32. In the event any other relevant document has been omitted to be placed before this court, the parties will be at liberty to circulate copies of the said papers to the other side and rely on the same at the time of final hearing of the appeal.

33. The learned Advocate-on-record for the appellant shall tender a server copy of this order on the learned Advocate-on-record for the respondent, indicating the returnable date as well, and file a receipt in that regard on the returnable date.
